newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Central Bank warns of liquidity bubble.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Central Bank warns of liquidity bubble.

text.p: Venezuela's money markets should experience a bubble liquidity in coming weeks which will hamper the Central Bank's efforts to tighten up monetary policy, Central Bank Director Carlos Hernandez Delfino said.
"We are expecting in the next few weeks an important increase in liquidity due to expenditures by the government and (state oil company) Petroleos de Venezuela," Hernandez told Union Radio.
"There is a strong monetary expansion due to these two sources and this obviously places additional restrictions on monetary policy," he added.
Hernandez did not specify what the PDVSA and government payments were.
The Central Bank plans to start issuing treasury bills on behalf of the government in August as an additional monetary tool.
But Hernandez said the appearance of the treasury bills would not mean the immediate disappearance of the Central Bank's Monetary Stabilization (TEM) bills.
Apart from the growing liquidity problems, the size of the outstanding TEM bills -- which Hernandez placed at 2.5 trillion bolivars ($5.1 billion) -- could not be substituted quickly.
